cohort: 8,426 pregnant women who delivered at King Fahad National Guard Hospital in Riyadh in 2021, with a focus on 341 obese women meeting specific inclusion criteria
finding: The study found a high prevalence of obesity (40.5%) among the pregnant women, with obesity significantly associated with adverse maternal outcomes (gestational diabetes, cesarean deliveries) and unfavorable fetal outcomes (lower APGAR scores, macrosomia).
mod_finding: The study found that obesity was associated with increased rates of cesarean deliveries.
